status_vocabulary.sourced: Transcribed from a specific table or statement in the cited reference.
status_vocabulary.textbook: Standard textbook value or range, cited to the chapter that states it.
status_vocabulary.approximate: Order-of-magnitude or approximate value; treat as indicative only.
status_vocabulary.model: Model parameter chosen inside the cited biological range, or derived from sourced values.
status_vocabulary.illustrative: Visual representation only; carries no quantitative claim.

structures.name: Plasma membrane
structures.summary: Lipid bilayer with embedded and associated proteins that encloses the cell and separates the cytoplasm from the extracellular environment. It controls the exchange of ions and molecules and carries the receptors that let the cell sense its surroundings.
functions: Ion gradients maintained by pumps such as the Na+/K+-ATPase
Hepatocyte surface specialized into sinusoidal (basolateral), lateral and canalicular (apical) domains
structures.render_notes: Drawn as a single translucent ellipsoid surface. Bilayer thickness is not to scale. The polyhedral shape of hepatocytes in tissue, microvilli and bile canaliculi are not modeled.

structures.name: Cytosol
structures.summary: The aqueous, protein-dense part of the cytoplasm outside membrane-bound organelles. Most protein synthesis on free ribosomes and many metabolic pathways, including glycolysis, take place here.
structures.render_notes: Not drawn as geometry; it is the space between rendered structures.

structures.name: Nucleus
structures.summary: Membrane-bounded compartment containing the chromosomes. It is enclosed by the nuclear envelope, two concentric membranes perforated by nuclear pore complexes; the outer nuclear membrane is continuous with the endoplasmic reticulum.
functions: Storage and replication of the nuclear genome
Regulated nucleocytoplasmic transport through nuclear pores

quantities.label: Number per hepatocyte (table value)
quantities.note: Hepatocytes are often binucleate or polyploid; the model uses one nucleus.

structures.render_notes: The nuclear envelope is drawn as one translucent ellipsoid surface. The two membranes and the perinuclear space (tens of nm) are not resolved at whole-cell scale.

structures.name: Nucleolus
structures.summary: Membraneless nuclear body that forms around ribosomal RNA genes. Ribosomal RNA is transcribed, processed and assembled with ribosomal proteins into ribosomal subunits here.
structures.render_notes: Number and size of nucleoli are illustrative.

structures.name: Nuclear pore complex
structures.summary: Large protein assembly built from about 30 different nucleoporins that spans both nuclear membranes. It allows passive diffusion of small molecules and selective, receptor-mediated transport of macromolecules.
functions: Export of mRNA and ribosomal subunits
structures.render_notes: Each pore is a small torus about 0.12 µm across. Rendered count is inside the textbook range.

structures.name: Chromatin
structures.summary: DNA packaged with histones and other proteins. Each nucleosome core wraps 147 nucleotide pairs of DNA around a histone octamer. Densely packed heterochromatin is enriched at the nuclear periphery and around nucleoli.
functions: Packaging and protection of the genome
structures.render_notes: Point cloud enriched toward the envelope and around nucleoli. Illustrative only.

structures.name: Rough endoplasmic reticulum
structures.summary: Ribosome-studded ER membrane sheets, continuous with the outer nuclear membrane. Secreted and membrane proteins are co-translationally inserted, folded and glycosylated here. In hepatocytes it makes plasma proteins such as albumin.

quantities.label: ER membrane share of total membrane (typical animal cell)

markers.protein: Protein transport protein Sec61 subunit alpha isoform 1

structures.render_notes: Three fenestrated perinuclear sheets carrying bound ribosomes. The geometry shows the arrangement only; its rendered volume is not matched to the 9% reference.

structures.name: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum
structures.summary: Ribosome-free ER, often tubular. It synthesizes lipids and stores Ca2+. In hepatocytes it is a major site of drug and xenobiotic metabolism by cytochrome P450 enzymes and of glucose-6-phosphatase activity.

quantities.label: Share of hepatocyte volume (smooth ER + Golgi cisternae, combined)

structures.render_notes: Tubular network with three-way junctions, drawn as lines. Illustrative; not volume-matched.

structures.name: Golgi apparatus
structures.summary: Stacks of flattened cisternae with a cis face receiving material from the ER and a trans face sorting it onward. In mammalian cells, stacks are linked laterally into a ribbon close to the nucleus and centrosome.
functions: Glycosylation and processing of proteins and lipids

quantities.label: Share of hepatocyte volume (smooth ER + Golgi, combined)

structures.render_notes: Curved cisternae coloured from cis (pale) to trans (deep gold), arranged around the centrosome. Cisterna diameter is illustrative.

structures.name: Transport vesicles
structures.summary: Small coated or uncoated vesicles that carry cargo between the ER, Golgi cisternae, endosomes and the plasma membrane.
structures.render_notes: Small spheres near the Golgi. Count and size are illustrative.

structures.name: Mitochondrion
structures.summary: Double-membrane organelle that carries out oxidative phosphorylation. It has its own genome, which in humans is 16,569 bp. In hepatocytes, mitochondria also run fatty-acid beta-oxidation, ketogenesis and the first steps of the urea cycle.

markers.protein: Mitochondrial import receptor subunit TOM20 homolog

structures.render_notes: Capsules whose count and total volume reproduce Table 12-2 exactly. Cristae, branching and fission/fusion networks are not modeled.

structures.name: Lysosome
structures.summary: Acidic, membrane-bounded degradative compartment containing about 40 types of hydrolytic enzymes that are active at low pH.
functions: Degradation of macromolecules from endocytosis and autophagy
structures.render_notes: Spheres whose count and total volume reproduce Table 12-2.

structures.name: Peroxisome
structures.summary: Single-membrane organelle without its own genome. It oxidizes very-long-chain fatty acids, produces and degrades hydrogen peroxide with catalase, and starts plasmalogen synthesis.
structures.render_notes: Spheres whose count and total volume reproduce Table 12-2.

structures.name: Endosome
structures.summary: Membrane-bounded sorting compartments that receive endocytosed material. Cargo is recycled to the plasma membrane or passed through progressively more acidic endosomes to lysosomes.
functions: Sorting of endocytosed receptors and ligands
structures.render_notes: Spheres whose count and total volume reproduce Table 12-2. Early and late endosomes are not distinguished.

structures.name: Ribosomes
structures.summary: The 80S eukaryotic ribosome is made of a 40S and a 60S subunit, built from four rRNAs (18S, 28S, 5.8S, 5S) and about 80 proteins. It translates mRNA into protein, either free in the cytosol or bound to the rough ER.
functions: Co-translational targeting to the ER (bound ribosomes)
structures.render_notes: Screen-space points. Only a sample is drawn (bound on rough-ER sheets, free in small polysome clusters); the real count is orders of magnitude higher.

structures.name: Centrosome
structures.summary: The main microtubule-organizing centre of animal cells. A pair of orthogonal centrioles, each a cylinder of nine triplet microtubules, sits in pericentriolar material that holds gamma-tubulin ring complexes, which nucleate microtubules.
structures.render_notes: Two orthogonal centrioles of 9 x 3 microtubules inside a translucent pericentriolar cloud. PCM size is illustrative.

structures.name: Microtubules
structures.summary: Hollow polymers of alpha/beta-tubulin, 25 nm in outer diameter and usually built from 13 protofilaments. In interphase they radiate from the centrosome, minus ends inward and plus ends toward the periphery, and serve as tracks for kinesin and dynein motors.
functions: Tracks for organelle and vesicle transport
Positioning of the Golgi and ER
structures.render_notes: Lines with an exaggerated on-screen width. Paths are routed around the nucleus. Count and curvature are illustrative.

structures.name: Actin cortex
structures.summary: A thin meshwork of actin filaments under the plasma membrane. It sets the cell's mechanical properties and drives shape change, endocytosis and membrane protrusions.
structures.render_notes: Short tangential segments just inside the membrane. Density and segment length are illustrative.

structures.name: Keratin intermediate filaments
structures.summary: Rope-like filaments about 10 nm in diameter that give cells mechanical resilience. Hepatocytes express keratins 8 and 18, which protect them against mechanical and toxic stress.
structures.render_notes: Wavy lines from the nuclear surface to the cortex. Illustrative.
